summary: Dale S. Wright specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He studied under Alan Anderson, Wei Pachow, and Robert Scharlemann, and served as David B. and Mary H. Gamble Professor of Religious Studies and Asian Studies at Occidental College around 1978.

Dalsukh D. Malvania worked in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies after studying under Sukhlal Sanghvi. He held an attested post at Banaras Hindu University in 1951 and served as Director of the Lalbhai Dalpatbhai Institute of Indology (attested 1965–1971).
Damchö Gyatso studied under Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse, Penor Rinpoche, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev worked in Tibetology and linguistics, having studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from Lancaster University and a D.Phil. from the University of Oxford, later becoming Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London around 1989.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi worked in Indology and history/archaeology. After studying at Harvard under George David Birkhoff, he held mathematics professorships at Banaras Hindu University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research (1945–1962), among other posts.

Dan Arnold works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned degrees from Carleton College, Columbia University, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago, and later taught at McGill University and the University of Chicago Divinity School (2004–2011).

Dan Lusthaus specializes in Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning a Ph.D. from Temple University under scholars including Charles Wei-hsun Fu and Bimal Krishna Matilal. He taught at institutions including Grinnell, Florida State, Georgia, and Harvard.

Dan Martin specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University, studying under Elliot Sperling, and held posts at the Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters, the Hebrew University of Jerusalem, and Carnegie Mellon University.

Dan Smyer Yü specializes in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He completed a PhD at the University of California, Davis, and served as a Research Group Leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who completed his PhD at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and a habilitation at the University of Copenhagen. He became a professor at Copenhagen in 2002 and was a professor of philosophy at Oxford (2018–2021).

Daniel A. Getz specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein and later served as an associate professor at Bradley University (attested 2019).
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned a doctoral degree from the University of Bristol under the supervision of Paul Williams.

Daniel B. Stevenson works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. After receiving his Ph.D. from Columbia University, he held assistant professorships at Butler University (attested 1986) and the University of Kansas (attested 1996–2003).
Daniel Borengasser is a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology. He completed a Master of Arts degree at the University of Oregon under the supervision of Akiko Walley, attested in 2014.

Daniel Boucher specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Indiana University and the University of Pennsylvania, where he completed his doctorate under Victor H. Mair, and served as Associate Professor at Cornell University (attested 2000–2008).

Daniel Clarke Waugh works in Iranian and Central Asian studies and history/archaeology. He earned degrees from Yale University and Harvard University before taking up a post at the University of Washington in 1972.

Daniel Coit Gilman studied at Yale, Cambridge, and Berlin. He served as librarian at Yale (1856–1872), president of the University of California (1872–1875), founding president of Johns Hopkins University (1875–1901), and president of the Carnegie Institution for Science (1902–1904).

Daniel Cozort is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and served on the faculties of Bates College (~1987–1988) and Dickinson College (~1988).
Daniel Dubuisson works in religious studies, history/archaeology, and Indology. He served as a director of research at the CNRS around 1980 and at the University of Lille (attested 2010).
